chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Khālid, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in the bathhouse. He said: If it is a clean place, then there is no harm in it.

So the correct way regarding this report is that we understand it as referring to the dressing area of the bathhouse, or as a kind of concession, because doing that is disliked, though not prohibited.

key_terms.الرُّخْصَةِ: a concession or dispensation in the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship under discussion
key_terms.بَيْتِ الْحَمَّامِ: the bathhouse, the location being asked about
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating permissibility
key_terms.مَكْرُوهٌ: disliked, meaning not preferred though not sinful
key_terms.مَوْضِعًا نَظِيفًا: a clean spot, the condition for permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in a bathhouse if the place is clean?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) in a bathhouse. The Imam عليه السلام permits it when the place is clean, while the closing legal clarification explains that this is to be understood either as referring to the changing area or as a concession, since praying there is disliked rather than forbidden.
